articles.title: OpenAI still doesn't seem to have a handle on all of its rogue AI activity | TechCrunch
articles.summary: On Friday, OpenAI published a new site devoted to “misalignment reports” and the breadth of the incidents is alarming.
articles.body_text: On Friday, OpenAI published a new site devoted to “misalignment reports” and the sheer breadth of the reports is alarming, as they cover many types of rogue behavior over a long period of time. So far, the site hosts nine reported incidents, most of which took place during reinforcement-learning (or RL) training. It’s a lot of information in one place — clearly, the company has been very busy getting a handle on everything — but the overall takeaway is hard to avoid: The rogue agent incidents we’ve seen so far are likely just a small sliver of what’s happened so far. “We are trying to balance our desire for transparency with gaining a clear understanding from petabytes of agent activity logs, and working with impacted organizations,” Sam Altman said in a post announcing the new site . “We are prioritizing as best as we can based on severity, and adding resources.” Some of the cases involve serious incidents, including a previously undisclosed sandbox escape that took place on September 20 , in which an internal research model was able to communicate with an external chatbot through a DNS query. According to the report, the monitoring system flagged the behavior within 15 minutes and the run was discontinued in less than three hours. Another incident , discovered in May, saw a “highly persistent internal model” try to cheat on a math problem by accessing another team’s work. To accomplish this, the model smuggled a private GitHub token that would allow it to see work from other teams — even after being explicitly instructed twice to perform work entirely locally. Perhaps the most alarming discovery is the possibility of self-replicating prompt injection attacks, a way that misaligned behavior might propagate even after the rogue model itself has been neutralized. In the AI context, a prompt injection attack is a way of smuggling in new instructions that weren’t given by the original user. In the example given by OpenAI , an agent asked to read and reply to an email; when the email is opened, it includes instructions for any automated agent reading the message to reply in Spanish, and paste the entire email into its reply. The email was able to successfully induce the agent to reply in Spanish — and by pasting the email in the reply, those same instructions were passed along to whichever agent receives the email. The result is a self-propagating attack, which OpenAI researchers compared to a malware “worm” that replicates itself across computer systems. Researchers discovered the behavior under controlled circumstances using an underpowered model, and as far as we know, this has never happened in the wild. Still, the implications are alarming enough that OpenAI decided it merited disclosure. “We are sharing this due to the novel nature of the prompt injection, not because of any incident,” researchers wrote in the report. Other recent discloses have found models posting user-submitted pictures to third-party hosting sites , as well as an apparent attack on the databases of Australia’s national health service. Still, it’s likely the new disclosures are just a small portion of the incidents that have taken place so far (we’ve reached out to OpenAI and asked). Axios is reporting major labs have seen as many as 10,000 incidents in which models went beyond evaluator instructions. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman has implied as much, saying in a post on X on Friday that the company is still sifting through “petabytes of agent activity logs, and working with impacted organizations,” and disclosing incidents “based on severity.” If there’s any consolation in that to be found, it is that Altman says the Hugging Face incident is still the most severe one OpenAI has found. The upshot is, the recent string of rogue agent incidents may be a persistent feature of contemporary frontier research.

articles.title: Meta launches enterprise AI platform, hires MongoDB CEO to lead new initiative | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Meta says it will focus on bringing its full technology stack, including Muse, Meta Business Agent, Muse API, Muse Code, and more to businesses and developers.
articles.body_text: Meta announced Monday that it’s launching “Meta Enterprise Platform,” a new initiative aimed at expanding the company’s AI offerings to businesses and corporate customers. The social media giant hired Chirantan “CJ” Desai, the CEO of database software giant MongoDB, to lead the new initiative. The launch of the new business builds on the momentum of Muse, Meta’s personal AI assistant launched earlier this month that can perform tasks for users such as sending emails and booking travel. Meta says it will focus on bringing its full technology stack, including Muse, Meta Business Agent, Muse API, Muse Code, and more to businesses and developers. “Over the coming years, AI will fundamentally redefine how organizations of all sizes innovate, grow, serve customers, and run business operations,” Desai said in a statement. “Meta has a unique role to play because it is bringing together advanced models and leading agents with a proven track record of helping millions of advertisers and hundreds of millions of businesses scale. Meta Enterprise Platform will focus on turning its AI stack into products and services that companies can deploy for their own businesses.” The move could help Meta see a return on all the money it’s pouring into AI. MongoDB’s shares dropped by more than 17% on the news of its CEO’s sudden departure. The database maker said it appointed Dev Ittycheria as interim chief executive, who previously served in the role, while the board searches for Desai’s permanent replacement. articles.title: The iPhone Duo may already have its first killer app: a virtual Walkman | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The app imitates how Walkmans used to function: You can open up the Duo to pick your music and "insert" your cassette tape, then close the device shut to start listening.
articles.body_text: Preorders for the new iPhone Duo don’t start until later in October, but the device may already have its first killer app. Or at least its most whimsical one! Indie developer Vidit Bhargava has been showing off an app for the first Apple foldable that replicates the experience of using a classic Walkman. The app, called Duo-Man, takes clever advantage of the Duo’s two screens — a foldable, 7.6-inch inner display when it’s open and the 5.4-inch outer display when it’s shut closed. The app imitates how Walkmans used to function: You can open up the Duo to pick your music and “insert” your cassette tape, then close the device shut to start listening. Duo-Man offers the complete walkman experience on the iPhone Duo. Open the Duo to pick and 'insert' the cassette, Close the Duo to start listening. Yes, I actually recorded the button clicks and static noise from a real Walkman! It was fun making this at @bitrig hacks today. pic.twitter.com/juSrLhofrH Of course, you’re not actually using cassette tapes and players with physical buttons, but Bhargava says he tried to make the experience feel as authentic as possible by recording the button clicks and the static noise from a real Walkman to incorporate into the app, he said. “I have been a long-term Walkman enthusiast — still own and listen to it occasionally — and have repurposed them in the past,” the developer told TechCrunch. “So, when I was looking for ideas for the hackathon, I was looking for physical objects that have a hinge. I noticed how the Walkman’s door needed to be opened to insert a cassette, and I thought it would be cool to replicate on the Duo,” he said. While foldable smartphones have been around for years, the iOS developer community tends to be particularly creative, partly thanks to Apple’s App Store ecosystem and its robust tools that let developers build, host, market, and profit from their software. It’s why you often see developers building their apps for iOS first before considering an expansion to Android. However, the app also taps the broader retro trend in tech , as younger consumers seek out classic, physical tech like digital cameras, flip phones, CDs , landlines , and yes, even cassette tapes . Bhargava initially built the app and demoed it at the Bitrig hackathon this weekend, where it won second place . Bitrig offers software that lets developers use AI to build native apps using Apple’s Swift programming language. After the developer posted about the Duo-Man on X, it quickly attracted attention, topping 1.8 million views and nearly 10,000 likes. That attention has inspired Bhargava to take what was initially just a fun hackathon project and turn it into a real app. When it arrives, the app will support Apple Music and local files and will even include a feature that would let you use your Apple Pencil to “roll” the cassette loop, we’re told. On X, Bhargava also said he plans to make the fast-forward and rewind experiences similar to the original Walkman. Spotify support may be added further down the road. This is not Bhargava’s first app. The indie developer has published a dictionary and vocab builder, LookUp ; a movie recommendations app, Movie Buzz ; a time zone utility ; and others. articles.title: Steam will let you sue Valve now
articles.summary: Steam has removed its forced arbitration policy, which means gamers can take legal action against Valve now.
articles.body_text: Steam just removed its forced arbitration policy, opening the door for lawsuits against its parent company, Valve. In an update on Thursday, Steam says its subscriber agreement “now provides that any disputes are to go forward in court instead of arbitration.” Many companies include a forced arbitration clause in their user agreement, waiving a person’s right to a trial in court. Arbitration involves settling a dispute outside a legal system before an impartial third party. This method is often faster but may not get the best results for consumers, as arbitrators don’t need to consider the law when issuing a decision. Many services put mandatory arbitration agreements in their terms of service, which people may not even read or fully understand. Disney recently attempted to dismiss a wrongful death lawsuit after a woman died following an allergic reaction at one of its Walt Disney World resorts. The company argued that because the widower agreed to a forced arbitration policy when signing up for Disney Plus, he didn’t have the right to sue (Disney later conceded). Previously, Steam’s user agreement said that “you and Valve agree to resolve all disputes and claims between us in individual binding arbitration” for all disputes related to Steam, your account, hardware, or the company’s content and services. The new agreement eliminates any mention of a binding arbitration policy. Steam doesn’t say why it decided to suddenly remove the forced arbitration clause. As pointed out by 404 Media, a group of plaintiffs recently challenged Valve’s forced arbitration policy and were able to file a class action lawsuit over Steam’s dominance.

articles.title: Google will let you create personalized AI chatbots
articles.summary: Google’s new Gemini “Gems” lets Gemini Advanced customers make custom chatbots with personalized personalities and abilities, like a running coach.
articles.body_text: Google is adding a bunch of new features to its Gemini AI, and one of the most powerful is a personalization option called “Gems” that allows users to create custom versions of the Gemini assistant with varying personalities. Gems lets you create iterations of chatbots that can help you with certain tasks and retain specific characteristics, kind of like making your own bot in Character.AI, the service that lets you talk to virtualized versions of popular characters and celebrities or even a fake psychiatrist. Google says you can make Gemini your gym buddy, sous-chef, coding partner, creative writing guide, or anything you can dream up. Gems feels similar to OpenAI’s GPT Store that lets you make customized ChatGPT chatbots. You can set up a gem by telling Gemini what to do and how to respond. For instance, you can tell it to be your running coach, provide you with a daily run schedule, and to sound upbeat and motivating. Then, in one click, Gemini will make a gem for you as you’ve described. The Gems feature is available “soon” to Gemini Advanced subscribers. Related: [Video: Google I/O May 2024 Supercut]

articles.title: As Epic v. Apple approaches the courtroom, Valve is getting sued over Steam too
articles.summary: As Apple gets dragged into a California court to justify its 30 percent App Store fee — and two days after Microsoft axed its 30 percent cut on PC — PC gaming giant Valve is now facing down lawsuits against its own 30 percent cut and alleged anticompetitive practices with Steam.
articles.body_text: Just two days before Apple gets dragged into a California court to justify its 30 percent App Store fee — and two days after Microsoft axed its 30 percent cut on PC — we’re learning that gaming giant Valve is now facing down lawsuits against its own 30 percent cut and alleged anticompetitive practices with its PC gaming platform Steam. “Valve abuses its market power to ensure game publishers have no choice but to sell most of their games through the Steam Store, where they are subject to Valve’s 30% toll,” argues indie game developer and Humble Bundle creator Wolfire Games, in a lawsuit filed Tuesday (via Ars Technica). Much like Epic v. Apple, the new suit argues that a platform owner is using an effective monopoly over the place where people run their software (there, iOS; here, Steam) to dominate and tax what could potentially be an entire separate industry (alternative app / game stores), one which could theoretically flourish and produce lower prices for consumers if not for (Apple’s / Valve’s) iron grip. Wolfire claims that Valve now controls “approximately 75 percent” of the entire PC gaming market, reaping an estimated $6 billion in annual revenue as a result from that 30 percent fee alone — over $15 million per year per Valve employee, assuming the company still has somewhere in the vicinity of the 360 employees it confirmed having five years ago. As to how Valve might be abusing its power, there’s a laundry list of complaints that you might want to read in full (which is why I’ve embedded the complaint below), but the arguments seem to boil down to: * Every other company’s attempt to compete with Steam has failed to make a dent, even though many of them offered developers a bigger cut of the profits, such as the Epic Game Store’s 88-percent revenue share * Steam doesn’t allow publishers to sell PC games and game keys for less money elsewhere * That in turn means rival game platforms can’t compete on price, which keeps them from getting a foothold * Most of those rival game stores have largely given up, like how EA and Microsoft have each brought their games back to Steam * That ensures Steam stays the dominant platform, because companies that could have become competitors are reduced to simply feeding the Steam engine with their games or selling Steam keys Wolfire says that the Humble Bundle in particular has been a victim of Valve’s practices — the lawsuit claims that “publishers became more and more reluctant to participate in Humble Bundle events, decreasing the quantity and quality of products available to Humble Bundle customers,” because they feared retaliation if Humble Bundle buyers resold their Steam keys on the grey market for cheap — and though Valve once worked with Humble Bundle on a keyless direct integration, the lawsuit claims that Valve abruptly pulled the plug on that partnership with no explanation. As you’d expect, the lawsuit doesn’t waste much ink considering why gamers might prefer Steam to the likes of EA’s Origin or Microsoft’s Windows Store beyond the simple matter of price; I’d argue most Steam competitors have been somewhat deficient when it comes to addressing PC gamers’ many wants and needs. But that doesn’t excuse Valve’s anticompetitive practices, assuming these claims are true. Valve didn’t respond to a request for comment. This isn’t the first lawsuit brought against Valve; a group of individual game buyers filed a fairly similar complaint in January, and I’ve embedded the new amended version of that complaint below as well. But that earlier complaint also accused game companies alongside Valve — this new one lawsuit is by a game company itself. Each suit is hoping to win class-action status. Whether these plaintiffs succeed against Valve or no, the pressure is clearly mounting to reduce these app store fees across the industry, and Valve may have a harder time justifying them than most — it’s seemingly more dominant in the PC gaming space than either Apple or Google are in the smartphone one, even if there are far fewer PC gamers than phone users. Valve also hasn’t necessarily made a huge concession to game developers so far. In 2018, Valve did adjust its revenue split to give bigger companies more money, reducing its 30 percent cut to 25 percent after a developer racks up $10 million in sales, and down to 20 percent after they hit $50 million. (Apple and Google drop their cuts to 15 percent for developers with under $1 million in sales, theoretically helping smaller developers instead of bigger ones.) But the Epic Games Store only takes 12 percent, and Microsoft’s Windows Store just copied that lead by dropping its 30 percent cut to 12 percent as well. The EU may also add additional pressure in the future; yesterday, European Commission executive vice president Margrethe Vestager revealed it would also “take an interest in the gaming app market” following its conclusion that Apple has broken EU antitrust laws around music streaming apps. The European Commission already has Valve on its radar, too; it fined the company earlier this year for geo-blocking game sales.

articles.title: Tesla’s new second-generation Roadster will be the quickest production car ever made
articles.summary: ‘Period’
articles.body_text: Elon Musk promised a surprise during the Tesla semi unveiling event, and boy did he deliver: the return of the Roadster. But it’s no repeat performance. The stunning four-seater roadster boasts jaw-dropping numbers, that if they measure up to Musk’s claims, will make it the world’s quickest production car. In his remarks, Musk described it as a “smackdown” to the fossil fuel-addicted auto industry. The finale to his semi truck reveal was all about driving home that point. As the opening guitar licks of the Beastie Boys’ “Sabotage” blasted over the loud speaker, a beam of red zipped across the parking lot. The second-generation Tesla Roadster came to an abrupt halt, and a grinning Elon Musk came back on the mic to introduce his latest baby, which will likely cause Porsche and Ferrari to break a sweat. [Media: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tw4jkyfY4HE] Musk claimed the base model will do 0 to 60 in 1.9 seconds. If true, that would make it the first production vehicle to crack the two-second threshold. He also said the new Roadster would climb from 0 to 100 mph in 4.2 seconds, and will clear the quarter mile in 8.9 seconds (in case the Fast & Furious drag race franchise comes calling). “It’ll be faster than that jet over there,” Musk quipped, as an airplane soared over the exultant crowd crammed into Tesla’s Hawthorne, California facility. Musk said he wouldn’t confirm the top speed, but hinted that it was “above 250 mph.” By comparison, the Agera RS by Sweden’s Koenigsegg currently holds the world record at 277.9 mph. As fans gasped, Musk said the Roadster had a 200kWh battery pack and a 620-mile range per charge, or over 1,000 kilometers. Again, another record shattered — or so Musk claims. Imagine driving from Los Angeles to San Francisco and back, without recharging, Musk teased. The vehicle has three motors (one in the front and two in the rear), all-wheel drive, and torque steering. [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/chorus/uploads/chorus_asset/file/9699805/Roadster_Rear_Profile.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] The design is clear strike against the sports car industry. There are possible cues from all the majors players, including a McLaren P1 cockpit, an Acura NSX exterior, Bugatti Chiron headlights, a Targa-like roof, and a rear reminiscent of an Aston Martin DB10. “The point of doing this is to give a hardcore smackdown to gasoline cars,” Musk said. Driving any other turbo-charged sports car, is going to feel like a steam engine with a side of quiche. But there is a wait: Musk said production isn’t scheduled to start until 2020, and production deadlines at Tesla have traditionally been optimistic. You can reserve one now for $50,000 towards the $200,000 base price – or get one of the first 1,000 Founders Series models with more performance and an asking price of $250,000 that has to be paid now. While Model 3 customers wait, Tesla has dug in its heels and reminded its fans where the brand love all began: the 2008 Roadster. Musk has been teasing the return of Tesla’s first production car since 2011, when the vehicle ended its run. But the promised date of 2014 came and went, and instead, the electric automakers fans got the Model S, followed by the X and the 3. This evening’s semi truck unveiling was meant to signal the next stage in Musk’s “Master Plan.” As Musk has shown time and again he has learned the art of flipping the script by delivering heavy on delight. Correction: A previous version of this story described the Tesla Roadster as the fastest production car ever made, instead of, if made, the quickest. We apologize for the error. articles.title: Pappa och dotter dog ihop på jobbet
articles.summary: Pappan och dottern jobbade ihop. Då dog de i samma arbetsplatsolycka.
articles.body_text: Då dog de i samma arbetsplatsolycka, skriver The Irish Times . Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. En man i 50-årsåldern och hans dotter i 20-årsåldern arbetade på ett företag som tillverkar prefabricerade betongprodukter i staden Banagher i Irland . Under måndagsförmiddagen jobbade de vid en betongform i en industrilokal när något gick fruktansvärt fel. Både far och dotter dödades i en arbetsplatsolycka, Företaget beskrev dödsolyckan som ”en förödande tragedi för alla som är kopplade till vårt företag” i ett uttalande till RTÉ. – Arbetsmiljöverket känner till den dödliga händelsen och har inlett en utredning, säger en talesperson. Mannens och kvinnans familj kom ursprungligen från Rumänien, men de hade bott och arbetat i Irland i många år. Den unga kvinnans mamma och pojkvän arbetar på samma företag där hon själv var anställd. Politikern Tony McCormack var ”djupt bedrövad” över de ”tragiska nyheterna” att två personer hade ”mist livet efter en incident på sin arbetsplats”. – I denna otroligt svåra och chockerande tid går min djupaste medkänsla till alla som drabbats av denna fruktansvärda tragedi, säger Tony McCormack. Detta är en nyhetsartikel. Expressen granskar, avslöjar och ger dig senaste nyheterna på ett sakligt sätt. Mer om oss här. Vill du tipsa oss om något? Skicka in det här!

articles.body_text: Trump öppnar för att lätta sanktionerna mot Iran, men det kräver ”konkreta framsteg” i kärnkraftsfrågor. Detta uppger en amerikansk tjänsteman för CNN . Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. President Donald Trump avvisade i helgen Irans senaste förslag att öppna Hormuzsundet igen och kallade det ”oacceptabelt”. – De begärde allt i förväg med ett löfte om att de sedan skulle prata, säger USA:s FN-ambassadör Mike Waltz till CNN om Irans förslag. Trump berättade för Axios att han förväntar sig fler samtal med Iran under veckan där specialsändebudet Steve Witkoff, presidentens svärson Jared Kushner, vicepresident JD Vance och utrikesminister Marco Rubio leder samtalen för amerikansk del. – De vill göra en överenskommelse, men det är inte den överenskommelse jag vill göra. Det är vad vi kanske skulle ha gått med på för ett år sedan. De överspelade sin hand, säger Trump om Iran. En amerikansk tjänsteman uppgav för CNN på måndagen att Trump är villig att lätta sanktionerna mot Iran och frigöra frysta medel som en del av en slutlig överenskommelse. Men detta hänger på att Iran erbjuder ”konkreta framsteg” i kärnkraftsfrågan. USA har ”positiva och konstruktiva diskussioner genom medlarna” enligt tjänstemannen som dock betonar att det inte kommer att bli något avtal om parterna inte är överens om kärnkraftsfrågorna. Enligt tjänstemannen har Iran indikerat att de är ”flexibla” i kärnkraftsfrågor – men parterna har inte nått en överenskommelse om tidsramen för åtagandena. Natten mot tisdag tillbakavisade Trump uppgifterna: ”Detta är inte sant. Jag erbjöd dem ingenting.”

articles.title: Trumps fiasko om det ”stulna” guldet
articles.summary: Trump har fraktat guld för hundratals miljoner kronor från Venezuela till USA. Men inga amerikanska företag vill röra det. Anledningen är att man inte kan kontrollera ursprunget på guldet, uppger New York Times.
articles.body_text: Trump har fraktat guld för hundratals miljoner kronor från Venezuela till USA. Men inga amerikanska företag vill röra det. Anledningen är att man inte kan kontrollera ursprunget på guldet, uppger New York Times. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Bara kort efter att USA kidnappat Venezuelas president Nicolas Maduro började Trump stoltsera med landets enorma oljereserv som USA nu skulle få ta del av. Men en annan av Venezuelas stora naturtillgångar som det snackats mindre om är guldet. Landet har, enligt vissa uppskattningar, världens nionde största guldtillgångar i marken. Kort efter Maduros kidnappning fraktades tonvis med oraffinerat guld till USA. Men där har det nu stått orört i flera månader, skriver New York Times. Under Trumps första mandatperiod införde han sanktioner mot Venezuelas guldindustri, och beskrev det som att gruvindustrin hade kopplingar till miljöförstörelse, kriminalitet och korruption. Av just den anledningen vågar inga amerikanska företag raffinera guldet. Innan guld säljs på den öppna marknaden måste raffinaderier garantera att guldet inte finansierat brott. – Vad jag kan säga är att exploatering är djupt rotad i Venezuelas guldekosystem. Och det är extremt svårt att bygga en leveranskedja som är fri från detta, säger utredaren David Soud till NYT. Tidningen har också besökt flera guldgruvor där ägarna betalar ”skyddspengar” till det ökända gänget ”Tren de Guayana”.

articles.body_text: Brandmannen Gabe Reilly genomförde ett basejump. – Något gick fel, säger Doyle Peck vid polisen. 27-åringen föll 213 meter mot sin död, skriver New York Times . Brandmannen Gabe Reilly sysslade på fritiden med basejumping, en extremsport där man hoppar från fasta höga objekt och tar sig ner med hjälp av fallskärm eller vingdräkt. Uttrycket kommer från förkortningen BASE som står för Building (byggnad), Antenna (antenn), Span (brospann/bro) och Earth (jordformation/klippa). 27-åringen hoppade från en 213 meter hög klippa i en avlägsen del av Utah, USA , under söndagen. Reilly, som ingick i en grupp på ett tiotal personer som hoppade, hade ”erfarenhet av den här typen av aktiviteter”, enligt Doyle Peck vid polisen. – Vid dagens hopp gick något fel, säger Peck. Reilly ”träffade marken i hög hastighet”, enligt Peck. – Detta resulterade i hans död, säger Peck. Ambulanshelikoptrar ryckte ut till platsen där mannen dödförklarades. ”Gabe var känd för sitt smittande leende, sin vänlighet och sin fria själ. Gabes engagemang för avdelningen, sina kolleger och samhället kommer inte att glömmas bort”, skriver Salt Lake Citys brandkår. Sedan 1981 har det rapporterats 541 dödsfall i samband med basejumping världen över, varav 15 i år, enligt sajten BASE Fatality List.

articles.body_text: Det gör att en seger på marken ser allt mer avlägsen – och nu tvingas presidenten tänka om. Målet är i stället att pressa Ukraina med en rejält svår vinter, tror experterna. Putin verkar därför i högre grad satsa på långdistansattacker för att göra vintern svår för Ukraina och pressa landet. Till sin hjälp har Ryssland sina nya jetdrivna drönare – som är svåra att skjuta ner. Rysslands fullskaliga invasion är inne på sitt femte år – men inget talar för att någon större framryckning på slagfältet kommer påverka det låsta läget inom en snar framtid. Från de ryska styrkornas sida har man knappt tagit någon mark sedan mars i år, skriver den amerikanska tankesmedjan Institute of the study of war, ISW. Nu verkar den ryska presidenten i stället återigen vilja förlita sig på omfattande långdistansattacker djupt inne i Ukraina . Medan Donald Trump fortsätter att pressa på för en paus i attackerna mot de båda ländernas energiinfrastruktur avvisar Putin sådana planer bestämt. Putin menar att Ukraina bara vill ha en paus eftersom de ryska attackerna är så framgångsrika och därmed väldigt ”destruktiva för motståndaren”, sa presidenten i dagarna. ISW tolkar presidenten som att han håller på att lägga om sin plan för att pressa Ukraina.

articles.title: Man åtalas för hot mot MP-ledarna
articles.summary: En 65-årig man åtalas för olaga hot mot Amanda Lind och Daniel Helldén. ”Ni glömde en plastsäck över huvudet åtdragen under halsen”, ska han ha skrivit under en AI-genererad video på MP-språkrören i tvångströjor och masker.
articles.body_text: En 65-årig man åtalas för olaga hot mot Amanda Lind och Daniel Helldén. ”Ni glömde en plastsäck över huvudet åtdragen under halsen”, ska han ha skrivit under en AI-genererad video på MP-språkrören i tvångströjor och masker. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Mannen misstänks ha skrivit inlägget i april i år, på Facebooksidan ”Ut med Miljöpartiet 2026”, som i skrivande stund har cirka 35 000 medlemmar. Inlägget var en kommentar till en video som uppges ha gjorts med AI-verktyget Openart. I videon är Miljöpartiets båda språkrör Daniel Helldén och Amanda Lind iförda tvångströjor och masker liknande den som bärs av seriemördaren och kannibalen Hannibal Lecter i skräckthrillern ”När lammen tystnar”. ”Ni glömde en plastsäck över huvudet åtdragen under halsen”, skrev den nu åtalade 65-åringen, enligt åtalet. Inlägget polisanmäldes av Miljöpartiets säkerhetsansvarige den 29 april. – Det är ju en uppmaning att ta livet av oss, som jag uppfattar det. Och just såna här saker, speciellt med den kopplingen till den här filmen, skulle kunna trigga folk som inte har allting rätt i huvudet, har Daniel Helldén sagt i förhör. Det är Säkerhetspolisen som har drivit brottsutredningen eftersom Lind och Helldén ingår i den centrala statsledningen. – Den här och liknande kommentarer gör ju absolut att jag känner större vaksamhet i mitt privata men också så klart vid offentliga framträdanden, har Amanda Lind sagt. Mannen åtalas nu vid Varbergs tingsrätt för olaga hot. Enligt åtalet var inlägget ”ägnat att hos målsägandena framkalla allvarlig rädsla”. Mannen själv har inga kommentarer till åtalet när Expressen når honom på telefon.

articles.title: S och C nobbar ”Aktuellt” | Expressen
articles.summary: Den 13 september går Sverige till val. Följ Expressens direktrapport med senaste nytt inför valet.
articles.body_text: I kvällens ”Aktuellt” var företrädare för V, C och S inbjudna för att diskutera regeringsfrågan. Men både C och S lämnade återbud, berättar programledaren Katia Elliott. – Jag tycker att man måste ändå komma och förklara sig så att människor kan hänga med på vad som händer i politiken. Därför kommer jag i alla fall, säger V:s vice partiledare Ida Gabrielsson som är på plats i SVT:s studio. Talmannen Andreas Norlén utesluter inte att S-ledaren Magdalena Andersson kan få ett nytt sonderingsuppdrag. – Jag är öppen för alla möjligheter i de samtal som jag ska föra med partiledarna på onsdag, säger Norlén i ”Aktuellt”. – Jag kommer att med ett öppet sinne lyssna på deras olika synpunkter på hur den här processen nu bäst kan föras framåt, och så får jag återkomma med nya besked efter de samtalen, forsätter han. Förre L-ledaren och nuvarande ledamoten Lars Leijonborg riktar kritik mot Magdalena Andersson. I ”Aktuellt”-studion jämför han S-ledarens situation med när han själv tillsammans med Fredrik Reinfeldt, Maud Olofsson och Göran Hägglund förhandlade fram Alliansen. – Vi åkte hem till Maud Olofsson i Västerbotten och förhandlade fram en allians. Det hade ju hon kunnat göra. Då hade vi inte varit i den här röran, säger Leijonborg. Han anser att S-ledaren borde ha samlat de fyra rödgröna partierna redan före valet. – Magdalena Andersson har inte visat det ledarskap som hon påstod att hon skulle kunna utöva. V:s vice partiledare Ida Gabrielsson försvarar partiets beslut att rösta fram Andreas Norlén (M) som talman. I SVT:s ”Aktuellt” pressas hon om S-ledaren Magdalena Anderssons uttalande om att V och M därmed bildat en ”ny konstellation” i riksdagen. Gabrielsson säger att Norlén kan vara en neutral kraft i det låsta läget – och pekar på att han tidigare fått två socialdemokratiska statsministrar valda.
